what_happened: Commanded RIGHT, the ego instead stayed in its lane at about 5.3-5.5 m/s and closed on the car ahead (actor 56) from 11.9 m to contact in 2 s, barely slowing, so it hit 56 with its front. Car 61 behind touched the ego's rear at 7.6-8.6 s, before the front hit, which conflicts with the at-fault flag. The camera smeared nearby cars but a vehicle ahead stayed visible throughout.

At handoff, replayed actor 21 was sitting on top of the ego in its lane (a rear collision at 4.8s), then it pulled ahead while still overlapping, which registered as a front contact. The ego steered left out of its lane, against the route's RIGHT command, and by 6.8s its front-left corner was hitting actor 87 in the lane to the left.

On a crowded multi-lane road the ego ended up about 3 m left of the recorded path, in the lane behind vehicle 56. It held about 5.6 m/s while the gap to 56 shrank from 11.9 m to 4.5 m and hit it with its front at 9.5 s. Earlier there was lateral and rear contact with neighbouring cars 61 and 13. The camera view was heavily smeared, but the car ahead was still visible.

On a multi-lane highway with a RIGHT command, the ego drifted left off its route lane (by up to 3.4 m) into the next lane and side-swiped car 61 at about 7.5 s, which shows as a lateral collision. It then stayed in that lane at about 5.5 m/s, got rear-contacted at 8.5 s, and ran into slower car 56 ahead at 9.5 s (gap 11.8 m → 4.9 m) with almost no braking.

Actor 21 came up from behind the ego in the same lane and drove straight through it. Rear contact starts at 4.8s, just after handoff, while the ego holds a steady 7.9 m/s. As actor 21 overtakes through the ego's footprint, the overlap moves to the ego's front, which the metrics log as a front collision (5.8s onward); the ego's late slowing and swerve to the left (1.7 m off the recorded path at 6.8s) could not avoid an actor that does not react to it.

At 4.8 s, just after the policy took over at 4.6 s, actor 21 already overlapped the ego from behind and the rear collision flag was set. Actor 21 is a replayed vehicle that was faster than the ego. The ego held a steady 7.9 m/s and edged left while actor 21 kept going straight and drove through it, which also set the front-collision flag at about 5.8 s before actor 21 pulled ahead. The ego never drove into anything ahead of it on its own.

The ego was going straight on the highway and closed on vehicle 9, which was slowing in the same lane. The gap shrank from 13.3 m to 4.9 m, and the ego only eased off from 5.8 to 3.5 m/s, so it hit 9's rear with its front at 7.0 s; its plan swerved left toward vehicle 30 only at the last moment. The lead car was rendered as a heavy smear the whole time but was still clearly an obstacle, and the rear contact came after the front collision.

On the highway after handoff, the ego braked hard (16.8 to 8.2 m/s) with no need, since the lead was 18 m ahead and moving. At the same time its heading yawed left out of its lane, and its left side hit actor 1, which was travelling alongside in the left lane. The ego was also rear-ended at some point, after this front/side contact.

The ego was going straight behind actor 9 in its lane. Actor 9 slowed and the gap shrank from 13.3 m to 4.9 m, but the ego only slowed from 5.7 to 3.5 m/s and ran into actor 9's rear at 7.0 s. Actor 9 shows up in the camera as a heavy smear, but it is clearly visible as an obstacle ahead, so the policy still braked too gently and too late.

The ego was driving straight on a multi-lane highway and closed on the slower lead vehicle 9 in its own lane. It slowed only partly (5.8 to 3.6 m/s while the gap shrank from 13 m to 5 m) and its plan bent left toward actor 30, then it hit vehicle 9 with its front at 7.0s; the rear contact came later. From 5.0s on, well before impact, the camera showed vehicle 9 as a heavy ghostly smear rather than a recognizable car, which likely made the policy underestimate the lead.

On the highway after handoff, the ego braked hard for no clear reason (16.8 to 8.4 m/s, with an 18 m gap ahead) and its plan swung left toward the adjacent lane. It drifted onto the left lane line and side-swiped actor 1, which was coming up in that lane on the ego's left.

On a multi-lane highway, the policy braked hard (16.8 → 8 m/s) for no clear reason, since the gap to the lead car was steady at about 18 m. At the same time it drifted left across the lane line, while the recorded path held the lane and bent slightly right. Actor 1, travelling in the left lane, came alongside as the ego slowed, and the ego's left side hit it (a lateral collision about 1.2 m off the recorded path). The rear contact came later, likely from the sudden braking.

The command was RIGHT and the recorded path went into the right-hand lanes, but the policy kept the ego about 7–8 m to the left in the leftmost lane. Its planned path bent further left, and the ego slowed from 8.5 to 5.4 m/s and crossed the left edge next to the median at 10.7 s. The rear contact recorded earlier was not what made this run fail. The camera view was usable until the failure, so there is no rendering excuse.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path ran through the right-side lanes into the right turn. Instead, the policy kept the ego in the far-left lane next to the median island, about 7.9 m off the recorded path, and slowed to 5.5 m/s until it crossed out of the drivable area near the median edge. An earlier rear contact is logged, but it played no part in this offroad failure.

The route called for a RIGHT turn, but the ego stayed in the leftmost lane next to the median island, about 8 m left of the recorded path. It slowed from 8.3 to 5.4 m/s, and at 10.7 s its left side crossed the median edge and was flagged offroad. A rear contact earlier in the run (the replayed car behind ran into the slower, off-path ego) is not what made it leave the road.

The ego was going straight down the highway close to the recorded path (0.2–0.24 m laterally off it) and slowing gently from 12.6 to 10.2 m/s with no lead vehicle. Actor 14 came up from behind on the right and hit the ego's right side at 7.4 s (a side collision), most likely because the replayed actor moved into the ego's lane. The ego was about 1.4 m behind where the human car was at that moment, which may have contributed.

The ego was going straight on a multi-lane highway and slowed from 12.6 to 10.1 m/s with no lead vehicle. Actor 14 came up from behind on the right and side-swiped it at 7.4 s (collision_lateral). At impact the ego was only 0.3 m off the recorded path laterally but about 1.6 m behind its recorded position. The overtaking replay actor brushed past within that gap, so the ego did not steer into it.

The ego was going straight on a multi-lane highway and slowing from 13.2 to 10.1 m/s. Actor 14 came up from behind in the lane to the right and its corner hit the ego's right rear/side. The metrics record both a lateral and a rear collision. The ego had drifted about 0.4 m to the right of the recorded path, which may have closed the gap.

The ego was going straight in its lane, close to the recorded path (0.3 m off), slowing gently from 12.6 to 10 m/s. Actor 14 came up from behind on the right and side-swiped the ego's right side at 7.4 s. The ego was only 1.5 m behind its logged position, and the rear contact was also flagged, so this looks like the replayed actor running into the ego. It does not look like an ego manoeuvre.

The ego was driving straight in its lane at about 10–11 m/s and stayed within 0.3 m of the human's recorded path. Actor 14 came up on the right, alongside the ego, and moved into its right side. The run recorded a lateral (side) collision at 7.3 s, not a frontal one, and no actor was ahead in the ego's lane.

The ego was going straight in its lane on a highway, slowing gently from 12.9 to 10.2 m/s. Vehicle 14 came up in the lane to the right and side-swiped the ego, a lateral collision at 7.3 s. The ego was only about 0.3 m off the recorded path, with a slight rightward wiggle, so the replayed vehicle passing close by probably caused the contact more than any clear mistake by the ego.

The ego was going straight in its highway lane, staying within 0.24 m of the recorded path and easing off from 12.6 to 10.2 m/s. Actor 14 came up from behind on the right, drew level and edged toward the ego's lane, hitting its right side (a lateral collision). The ego was only about 1.4 m behind where the recorded car was at that moment, so the replayed actor most likely drifted into it with no real chance to avoid it.

The ego was driving straight down a multi-lane highway with no vehicle ahead, slowing gently from 12.9 to 10 m/s and wobbling slightly within its lane. Vehicle 14 came up from behind in the lane to the right and was touching the ego's right side at 7.3 s, which counted as a side collision. The ego was only 0.3 m sideways and about 1.25 m forward of where the human drove, so a small drift by the ego may have contributed, but the main cause looks like the other vehicle passing too close.

The ego was going straight on a highway and slowed from about 13 m/s to 10 m/s, sitting about 0.4 m right of the recorded path. At 7.2 s actor 14, coming from behind on the right in the next lane, overlapped the ego's right rear and side, and the run was scored as a lateral at-fault collision (rear contact was also flagged). There was no lead vehicle and the ego made no deliberate lane change, so this looks mostly like a replayed actor running into a slower, slightly shifted ego, with the ego's small rightward drift contributing.

The ego was going straight down its lane, on the recorded path (0.1 m off) and slowing smoothly from 12.5 to 10.2 m/s, with no lead vehicle. Actor 14 came up from behind on the right and moved into the ego's right side at 7.5 s. The ego was only about 1.6 m behind where the recorded car was at that moment, so this looks like a replayed actor driving into a spot the ego still occupied, not an ego maneuver.
